reason: Without fusion support, gravity should cause the iron-group core to collapse.
expectation: The core will collapse, beginning the star's final transformation.

effect: The iron-group core has collapsed, producing dense neutron-rich matter and escaping neutrinos.
reaction: The connection between collapse and neutron formation is interesting.
reason: The neutrino flood is the most plausible available ingredient for the next stage of the collapsing core, though I am guessing at the game's intended mechanism.
expectation: Neutrinos may help drive the explosion or transform the collapsing core.

effect: The neutrino flood helped produce an outward shock, which can now interact with the star's layers.
reaction: It is useful to see that this explosion mechanism is presented as one modeled route, not a universal outcome.
reason: The outward shock should carry the star's enriched shells into space.
expectation: The shock will scatter the enriched stellar layers.

effect: The shock scattered the enriched layers, completing that goal; the central remnant still needs to be found.
reaction: The distinction between material made during the star’s life and in the explosion is useful.
reason: The collapsing core is the clearest place to investigate the remaining central remnant.
expectation: Its available partners should indicate how to form or identify the remnant.

effect: The inspection automatically combined the core with gravity to produce a neutron star, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: I was interested that neutron-rich matter can resist further collapse, while a more massive remnant might become a black hole.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the neutrino flood with the collapsing core was most worthwhile: it connected energy deposition to the outward shock while making clear that this is one modeled explosion route.

leastWorthwhile.text: Finding the remnant was less engaging as a decision: inspecting the core revealed only one partner and performed the combination automatically.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the ejecta contain nuclei made both during the star’s life and in the explosion.

arbitrary.text: Using gravity again to turn the collapsing core into a neutron star felt somewhat abstract, although the result explained why this remnant resists further collapse.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the scattered stellar material becomes the rock and water described in the opening, especially if later combinations explain those processes as clearly.
